tools.concrete:
1. Home
  2. Site tools
  3. Concrete

Concrete calculator

How much concrete, how many mixer loads, how long the pour will take, and how many mixers must run to keep the pump from waiting.

On this page
  1. How it is worked out
  2. What it does not do
Site tools
  • Site tools overview

Calculators

  • Concrete
  • Reinforcement
  • Earthwork and haulage
  • Shutdown planner
  • Shift bus planner
  • Units of the site

How it is worked out

Volume
Length by width by depth, or the area of a circle by its height, times the number of identical pours. An allowance for wastage is added.
Mixer loads
Volume divided by what one transit mixer carries, rounded up.
Pour time
Volume divided by the pump’s output. A pump rarely holds its best rate for a whole pour, so treat this as the shortest it could be.
Mixers to keep the pump fed
In one round trip a mixer delivers one load. The pump empties that load in a few minutes. The number of mixers is the pump’s hourly output, times the round trip in hours, divided by one load.
Nominal mix
For small work, materials by volume. Dry volume is taken as 1.54 times the wet volume, and a 50 kg bag of cement as 0.0347 cubic metres.

What it does not do

It does not design a mix. Structural concrete of grade M 25 and above is proportioned by weight from a mix design, proved by trial. Indian practice allows nominal mixes only for M 20 and below, and on this coast most structural concrete is of a higher grade than that. See Civil and structural works.

It does not know about your access, your weather or your batching plant’s real output. See Mass concrete for what a large pour actually demands.

1. Home

Reinforcement calculator

The weight of reinforcing bars from their diameter and length, by the rule every bar bender in India knows by heart.

On this page
  1. The rule
  2. What it does not do
  3. Eight hundred tonnes
Site tools
  • Site tools overview

Calculators

  • Concrete
  • Reinforcement
  • Earthwork and haulage
  • Shutdown planner
  • Shift bus planner
  • Units of the site

The rule

A steel bar weighs its diameter in millimetres, squared, divided by 162, in kilograms for every metre.

A 12 mm bar: 12 times 12 is 144. Divided by 162 is 0.889 kilograms a metre. A standard 12-metre length weighs a little under 10.7 kilograms.

The rule comes straight from the density of steel, 7,850 kilograms a cubic metre, and it is accurate to within the rolling tolerance of the bar.

What it does not do

It does not add laps, hooks, chairs or wastage. A bar bending schedule does that, bar mark by bar mark. As a rough guide, laps and wastage commonly add a few per cent to the weight taken off the drawing.

It does not tell you whether a trailer may legally carry the load. That depends on the vehicle’s registered weight.

Eight hundred tonnes

On one plant expansion we coordinated the delivery of 800 tonnes of reinforcement. Enter a trailer load of 27 tonnes above and see how many journeys that is. Then consider that each had to arrive in the order the bar benders needed it. See A plant expansion.

Earthwork and haulage calculator

How much is in the ground, how much it becomes once it is dug, what it weighs, and how many tipper trips will carry it away.

On this page
  1. How it is worked out
  2. What it does not do
  3. Brass
Site tools
  • Site tools overview

Calculators

  • Concrete
  • Reinforcement
  • Earthwork and haulage
  • Shutdown planner
  • Shift bus planner
  • Units of the site

How it is worked out

Volume in the ground
Length by width by depth. For a trench with sloping sides, use the average width.
Swell
Dug material takes up more room than it did in the ground. We use a factor of 1.25 for soil and moorum, 1.4 for soft or weathered rock and 1.6 for broken basalt. These are typical. Measure your own after the first day.
Weight
Volume in the ground times a typical density: 1.8 tonnes a cubic metre for soil, 2.2 for soft rock, 2.9 for basalt.
Trips
The larger of two numbers: loose volume divided by the tipper’s body, and weight divided by its legal payload. With basalt it is nearly always weight that decides. A body full of broken basalt is an overloaded lorry.
Tippers needed
Trips, divided by the trips one tipper can make in a shift, divided by the number of shifts you have.

What it does not do

It does not allow for the excavator. A tipper fleet should be matched to the machine that loads it, so that neither waits for the other.

It does not allow for the weighbridge queue, the monsoon or the lions. See Bulk haulage.

Brass

Sand, stone and earth are sold across Gujarat by the brass. One brass is 100 cubic feet, or about 2.83 cubic metres. The loose volume above is shown in both.

Shift bus planner

Enter the people on each shift and the seats in a bus. The planner works out how many buses each shift change needs, and the size of fleet to contract.

On this page
  1. How it is worked out
  2. What it does not do
  3. From an estimate to a contract
Site tools
  • Site tools overview

Calculators

  • Concrete
  • Reinforcement
  • Earthwork and haulage
  • Shutdown planner
  • Shift bus planner
  • Units of the site

How it is worked out

At each change of shift a bus does two jobs. It brings the incoming shift to the gate and takes the outgoing shift home. So the number of buses at a change is set by the larger of the two shifts, divided by the seats, rounded up.

The same buses serve all three changes, so the fleet on the road is the largest of the three figures. General-shift staff usually travel at different hours and can use the same vehicles.

Behind the fleet stand the spares. We allow at least one, and one for every five buses in a larger fleet.

What it does not do

It treats everyone as living on the same route. Real routes are drawn from where people live, and a thinly populated route may need its own mini-bus however few ride it.

It does not allow for people who come on their own motorcycles, as many do.

It assumes nobody stands. On a highway route, nobody should.

From an estimate to a contract

Tell us where your people live and we will draw the routes, time the stops and propose a fleet. See Staff and shift transport.

1. Home

Units of the site

A site office in Gujarat works in cubic metres and in brass, in MPa and in kg/cm², in tonnes and in bags, and in lakh and crore. Head offices elsewhere work in millions. This converts between them.

On this page
  1. The units you will meet here
  2. Lakh and crore, for readers outside India
Site tools
  • Site tools overview

Calculators

  • Concrete
  • Reinforcement
  • Earthwork and haulage
  • Shutdown planner
  • Shift bus planner
  • Units of the site

The units you will meet here

Brass
100 cubic feet, or 2.83 cubic metres. The everyday measure for sand, stone and earth.
Cubic foot
Still used for timber, stone and small quantities. 35.3 to the cubic metre.
Bag
A bag of cement is 50 kilograms. Twenty bags make a tonne.
Quintal
100 kilograms. Used for steel in the market, and for crops.
MPa
The modern unit of concrete strength. M 30 concrete has a characteristic strength of 30 MPa, which is 30 newtons on every square millimetre.
kg/cm²
The older unit, still on many drawings and in many heads. One MPa is about 10.2 kg/cm².
Lakh
One hundred thousand. Written 1,00,000.
Crore
Ten million. Written 1,00,00,000. A hundred lakh.

Lakh and crore, for readers outside India

Indian figures are grouped differently. After the first three digits, commas come every two. So 2,500,000 is written 25,00,000 and read as twenty-five lakh.

Our safety record of 2.5 million man-hours is 25 lakh man-hours. A port expansion of ₹17,000 crore is 170 billion rupees.

Call first

The number is answered at any hour. It is on the Contact page, with WhatsApp and the address.

Contact

Five things we will ask

  1. Which plant, and which gate?

    So that people and machines go to the right one.

  2. Where inside?

    The area, the equipment and the level. “Kiln 2 inlet.” “CF silo top.” “Wagon tippler.”

  3. What has happened?

    Short and plain. What failed, and what is stopped.

  4. What do you need first?

    A crane. Fitters and welders. An excavator. A supervisor to look. If you do not know, say so, and we will send someone who does.

  5. Who do we ask for?

    A name and a mobile number at the plant.

While we are on the way

If you can, have these ready

What will happen

In the first five minutes
A supervisor who knows your plant, a machine and a crew are called. You receive a message with the supervisor’s name and number.
Within thirty minutes
Our first people are at your gate, anywhere in the Rajula, Jafrabad and Pipavav belt.
On arrival
Our supervisor reports to your shift in-charge, assesses, and raises the permit. No tool is lifted before that.
From then on
One voice gives you short, factual updates.

The full sequence is on The emergency protocol.

After you have called: send a note

A written note helps the crew that is already moving. It is optional. Call first.

This form needs JavaScript. You can also reach us from the Contact page.

Outside the belt

For sites beyond Rajula, Jafrabad and Pipavav we still come, and we will tell you honestly how long it will take.

If people are in danger

This desk is for plant and structural emergencies. If someone is hurt, trapped or in danger, raise your plant’s emergency alarm and call the ambulance on 108 before you call us.

What you can ask for help with

Wages not received, or short
Tell us the site, the month, your contractor and what you were paid. You are owed the full wage for the days you worked, on the date promised.
Provident fund (PF)
Your account number is called a UAN. It should be given to you, and your contributions should appear in your PF passbook. If you do not have a UAN, or nothing has been deposited, tell us.
State insurance (ESI)
You should have an insurance number, which entitles you and your family to treatment. If you do not have one, tell us.
Identity card or gate pass
Lost, expired or not issued.
Injury or illness at work
Every injury must be reported and treated. You are entitled to compensation as the law provides. Nobody may ask you to hide an injury.
Stay, food or water
If the place you were given to sleep, or the water at the site, is not fit.
Behaviour of a supervisor or contractor
Abuse, threats, or unfair treatment.
Someone asked you for money
For the job, the pass, the wage or anything else. That is forbidden. Tell us.
Documents kept from you
Nobody may keep your Aadhaar, certificate or passbook.

How to ask

  1. Tell your supervisor first, if you can

    Most things are settled the same day.

  2. If that does not work, or you do not wish to

    Fill in the page below, or call the number on the Contact page and say that you need the worker help desk.

  3. If it is serious, or you are afraid

    Use the speak-up page. It goes to the leadership. You need not give your name.

The worker help page

This form needs JavaScript. You can also reach us from the Contact page.

What happens next

  • Your request is read by someone who does not work on your site.
  • We check the attendance and wage records.
  • If you are owed money for work on our job, you are paid it. If a contractor has not paid you, we take it up with the contractor, and you do not have to.
  • You are told the result.
  • Nobody may punish you for asking. If anyone tries, tell the leadership.

You do not lose your place on the register for asking for what you are owed.

About the firm

What does ATKAYVA do?

Civil and structural works, mechanical erection, plant shutdowns and emergency repairs, heavy machinery and manpower supply, transport and heavy haulage, corporate fleet services and materials supply, for the cement works, the port and the heavy industry of the Saurashtra coast. See Capabilities.

Where are you based?

At Kovaya, in Rajula taluka of Amreli district, Gujarat. The village stands beside a large cement works and a few kilometres from Port Pipavav. See The ground beneath us.

How old is the firm?

Work began in 2015 with one excavator and a crew of six. See The decade, year by year.

What is a network organisation?

A lean core of our own people plans, supervises and answers for the work. The machines, most of the workforce, the transport and the specialist engineering come from long-standing partners who work to our standard. You deal only with us. See A network, by design.

Do you own the 300 machines?

No. They belong to owner-operators in our network who give our calls priority. We say so plainly on Numbers, and how we count them.

Are you certified to ISO or other standards?

We do not claim certifications we do not hold. Our safety system is aligned with international standards, and our records are open to a client’s audit.

Who are your clients?

We do not name them. See Why no client is named. We will arrange references during pre-qualification.

Where do I get your tax and registration details?

We send them with the vendor papers. Ask through Document requests.

Working with us

How do I ask for a price?

Use the enquiry page for a first conversation, or the request for quotation if you know the scope. Or call.

Do you visit the site before quoting?

Yes. No decision about a site is made by someone who has not seen it.

Can I take only one service, such as a crane or a crew?

Yes. Any single line of our schedule can be taken alone. See Ways to engage us.

What is the smallest job you will take?

There is no minimum. Most of our clients began with one small order.

Do you work outside Amreli district?

Yes, and we say honestly that the thirty-minute response applies only inside the Rajula, Jafrabad and Pipavav belt. Elsewhere we mobilise as any contractor does.

Who will I deal with?

One project manager, named at the start, with authority to act. See Project governance.

How will I know what is happening?

A progress report every day. See the specimen on Project governance.

What do you need from us?

Permits, isolations, inspections at each stage, and decisions on changes of scope. Everything else is ours. See The Zero-Interference Doctrine.

Will your people follow our safety rules?

Yes. Where your rule and ours differ, the stricter applies.

How do we register you as a vendor?

Ask for our documents through Document requests. See also Starting with a new client.

Emergencies

What number do I call in an emergency?

The number is on the Contact page. It is answered at any hour.

How fast will you come?

Within thirty minutes to site across the Rajula, Jafrabad and Pipavav belt.

Do I need a purchase order before you come?

No. We come first and settle the paper in the morning. It is quicker if call-out rates were agreed beforehand under a rate contract.

What will you ask me on the telephone?

Which plant and gate, where inside, what has happened, what you need first and who to ask for. See Emergency call-out.

Will you start work without a permit if it is urgent?

No. The permit is raised before a tool is lifted, at midnight as at noon.

What kinds of emergency do you handle?

Mechanical and civil failures, urgent excavation, lifting, extra hands, clearing of blockages and debris, and urgent movement of machines and material. See Emergency response.

Machines

What machines can you supply?

Excavators from 5 to 50 tonnes with rock breakers, bulldozers, mobile cranes up to 35 tonnes, crawler cranes, piling rigs, vibratory rollers, transit and self-loading mixers, concrete pumps and boom pumps. See Heavy machinery.

Do machines come with operators?

Always.

What happens if a machine breaks down?

It is repaired by the mechanical support team, or replaced from the network.

How is hire charged?

By the hour, shift, month or year, with the terms agreed in writing before the machine moves.

Can you break rock without blasting?

Yes. Heavy excavators with hydraulic breakers open basalt beside live plant. See Rock excavation.

Do your cranes have test certificates?

Cranes and lifting tackle carry current certificates, and the load chart is in the cab.

People

How many people can you provide, and how fast?

A core of 130 specialists, and more than 600 on the call-up register, deployable within 72 hours.

Which trades?

Fitters and millwrights, welders, riggers, electricians, masons, carpenters, bar benders, operators, supervisors, engineers and helpers. See Industrial manpower.

Are your welders qualified?

Our certified welders hold 6G and 4G qualifications, and every welder is tested by us before deployment.

Who pays the workers and handles PF and ESI?

We do, or the labour contractor does under our supervision, and we check. Records are available to the principal employer.

Are the workers local?

Nearly all. They live in the villages round the plants.

Do you employ anyone under eighteen?

No. See Labour standards.

Transport and fleet

What can you transport?

Aggregates, sand, limestone, clinker, coal, gypsum, cement, steel, fabricated structures, heavy machines and port cargo. See Transport and heavy haulage.

Do you handle customs clearance?

No. Your clearing agent does. We coordinate with the agent so that the trailer and the release arrive together.

Can you move an oversize load?

Yes, on low-loaders, with a route survey and the permissions the load requires. See Heavy and oversize moves.

Do you overload vehicles to save trips?

No. It is illegal and unsafe.

Can you run our shift buses?

Yes, on fixed routes and timings, with a spare behind every vehicle. See Staff and shift transport.

Do cars come with drivers?

Yes.

Can you pick up a visitor from Diu or Bhavnagar airport?

Yes. See Officer and visitor cars.

Safety and quality

What is your safety record?

More than 2.5 million man-hours since 2015 with no reportable lost-time incident. The definition is on Numbers, and how we count them.

Can any worker stop a job?

Yes. Nobody is punished for stopping work in good faith.

How do you test concrete?

Materials are tested at NABL-accredited laboratories before use. Cubes are cast from every pour and tested at 7 and 28 days.

Why does concrete need special care on this coast?

Because of salt. See What salt does to concrete.

What records will we receive?

Test certificates, signed inspection requests, pour cards, alignment protocols, as-built drawings and measurement sheets, in one handover file.

Has any structure you built failed?

No structural failure has been recorded in more than 60,000 cubic metres of concrete placed since 2015.

Money

How are jobs priced?

By item rates, by rate contract, as a package or by hire, depending on the work. See Ways to engage us.

Do you charge for a site visit or a quotation?

No.

Do you ask for or give commissions?

No. See Anti-bribery and gifts.

How do we pay you?

To the firm’s bank account, as notified on our letterhead and confirmed by telephone. Never to an account sent by message alone. See Fraud alert.

Will there be extra charges at the end?

No extra work is done without telling you first and getting your agreement.

Partners

How do I join your network?

Register on Register. We will come and see your machine, vehicle, crew or yard.

Is there a registration fee?

No. Nobody may charge you one.

When will I be paid?

On the date in your order, by bank transfer. See Payments.

What if someone from ATKAYVA asks me for money?

Do not pay. Tell the leadership through the speak-up page.

I have only one machine. Is that enough?

Yes. Many of our best partners are owner-operators.

Jobs

How do I apply for work?

On Apply, by telephone, or in person at Kovaya.

Do I have to pay anything?

No. Never. If anyone asks for money in our name, it is a fraud.

I have no certificate. Can I still apply?

Yes. Start as a helper and learn. See First jobs.

What is the call-up register?

A list of tested and verified workers who are called when there is work. See The call-up register.

My wage is late. What do I do?

Tell your supervisor, or use the worker help desk.

Do you hire women?

Yes. See Respect at work.

This website

I filled in a form. Has it been sent?

Not yet. The forms on this site prepare a message and show it to you. You then choose to send it by WhatsApp, by email or by post. Until you do, we have received nothing.

What is the reference number on my message?

It is made on your own device, so that you and we can point to the same message. It is not a receipt.

Does this site track me?

No. It uses no analytics and no advertising. It remembers your choice of day or night shift and any unsent form draft on your own device. See Privacy.

What is the day shift and night shift switch?

It changes the site between a light and a dark appearance. The lamps in the drawings come on at night.

Are the pictures real?

They are drawings made for this site. We do not publish photographs of clients’ plants.

Can I read the site in Gujarati or Hindi?

The most important pages for workers and partners are summarised in ગુજરાતી and हिन्दी.

Something on the site is wrong. Whom do I tell?

The helpdesk. See Helpdesk.

Did not find your question?

Ask it. If it is a good one, it will be added here.
